howItWorks.title: How AfriYield Exchange Works
howItWorks.subtitle: A transparent, step-by-step explanation of how we connect investors with African agriculture

simple.title: The Simple Version
simple.step1body: We identify and verify African agricultural cooperatives seeking investment for equipment and processing infrastructure.
simple.step2body: Diaspora and international investors choose opportunities that match their goals and commit capital through our platform.
simple.step3body: Investors receive bi-annual returns. Cooperatives grow their operations. Farmers earn more for their harvest.

detailed.title: The Detailed Version
detailed.a1: Every cooperative must submit registration documents, physical address, leader identification, and minimum member count before appearing on AfriYield Exchange. Our team reviews every application manually before activating any listing.
detailed.a2: Track A investments fund physical equipment owned by the cooperative — tractors, drying machines, cold storage. The equipment exists as tangible collateral. Track B investments are governed by a formal revenue-share agreement signed before any funds are transferred.
detailed.a3: Transformation centers submit production and sales reports twice a year — before June 1 and December 1. Returns are calculated from actual revenue data. Payouts are distributed in June and December via bank transfer, Zelle, WISE, or mobile money depending on the investor's location.
detailed.a4: For Track A investments, equipment can be recovered and sold to recover investor capital. We work with all parties to find resolution. Full protections are detailed in the investment agreement every investor signs before committing funds.
detailed.a5: AfriYield Exchange is operated by Djigui Corporation, founded by Isabelle Coulibaly. Learn more at djiguicorporation.org and isacoultess.com.

help.title: How can we help you?
help.subtitle: Tap a question below or send us a message

questions.q4: What is Track A or B?
questions.q5: How do I see my farmers?

answers.a1: You get paid twice a year — in June and December. We send you a message on WhatsApp and email 7 days before your money arrives.
answers.a2: Track A money buys real equipment — like a tractor or drying machine — that belongs to the cooperative. The equipment is always there as security. Track B is a revenue-share deal with a signed agreement.
answers.a3: Go to the 'My Portfolio' tab and tap 'Add more to this investment'. Or browse new opportunities and choose a different cooperative.
answers.a4: Track A means your money buys real equipment for farmers. It is the safer option. Track B means your money goes into growing and selling the brand of a product. It can earn more but takes longer.
answers.a5: In 'My Portfolio', tap 'See the farmers'. You will see the supply chain — from the farmer who grew the crop to the cooperative that processed it.
